review.summary:
Phase 3 ("Typed models and scanning") meets its acceptance criteria with unusually strong, genuinely independent, executed evidence, and every blocking finding from attempt 01 has been fixed in the reviewed source.

Implementation: `airs::scan::Scanner` implements all four frozen scan operations plus a typed `scan_request` escape hatch (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/scan/scanner.rs:65-176), with a transactional `Content` builder matching the baseline's falsy/byte-length semantics (content.rs:186-214 vs .local/typescript/src/scan/content.ts:57-77). Paths, region endpoints, ID/batch caps and HMAC header behaviour match the frozen source exactly. The representative slice adds an OAuth management read (profiles.rs:60-74, path/query identical to .local/typescript/src/management/profiles.ts:43-58), a bounded SSE chat stream (gateway/runtime.rs:60-81, streaming/sse.rs), and a non-UTF-8 binary download (runtime.rs:26-40). Request validation and normalization run before credentials or dispatch (engine.rs:362-384); HMAC signs the exact transmitted bytes and retries reuse them; POSTs and streams are never replay-safe.

Models/validation: 3,261 generated public types with Optional/Nullable/Patch presence states, FiniteNumber, redacted Debug everywhere, extension-collision rejection, and a data-driven Zod interpreter over all 13,018 frozen nodes with 69 source-hash-pinned semantic bindings. Generation is byte-exact reproducible under the gate.

Evidence verified, not trusted: docs/checks/phase-03.json records exactly the 26 commands that tools/check_phase.py:47-71 defines, all exit_code 0, source_sha256 18bcfea7… matching the reviewed SHA, source_unchanged true. Rust reports contain real cargo stdout (fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/doc) across 1.88.0 and 1.99.0 and default/minimal/all/json-unification/scan/management/gateway/models. tests/schema_contracts.rs compares all 60,271 oracle cases in both modes against actual frozen Zod execution and asserts the case count; a separate consumer crate round-trips 27,216 typed cases.

Residual findings are medium/low: the operation ledger marks gateway/management operations "implemented" from method-name presence alone, with no record of omitted baseline options or stricter-than-baseline rules; there is no structural guard that every string/number check kind and regex source in the graph is implemented natively (unknown ones silently reject-all); and public union enums use positional `VariantN` names. None of these contradict a phase-3 criterion or block advancement.

findings.description: The parity ledger derives `implementation: "implemented"` purely from a regex match on the Rust method name plus the existence of a test file, and overwrites `owningPhase` to 3 for every mapped operation. Two mapped operations are materially narrower than the baseline: `RuntimeClient::create_chat_completion`/`_stream` and `download_file` (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/gateway/runtime.rs:26-81) expose no equivalent of the baseline's `GatewayInferenceRequestOptions.headers` x-portkey-*/OpenAI-Beta routing option and its validation (.local/typescript/src/ai-gateway/inference-client.ts:91-98, 202-228), and `Scanner::async_scan`/`scan_request` enforce content invariants the frozen raw async path does not (scanner.rs:107-133). Those deviations exist only in prose (docs/SCANNING.md:18-20); contracts/native-operations.json carries no per-operation deliberate-difference or partial marker, and `owningPhase: 3` hides the gateway rows from a future phase-6 sweep for `owningPhase: 6`. A phase-6/7 reconciliation reading this ledger would conclude these operations are complete.
findings.required_fix: Add a per-mapping field (for example `deliberateDifferences` and/or `optionParity: "partial"`) to MAPPINGS and the emitted rows recording the omitted baseline request options and the stricter async content rule, and retain the family's real owning phase alongside the phase that delivered the representative slice (for example `owningPhase: 6, deliveredInPhase: 3`).

findings.description: `compact_graph` copies ZodString/ZodNumber `checks` verbatim into validation/schema_graph.json with no assertion that each check kind and each regex source is implemented natively. `check_string` (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:889-930) and `check_number` (931-967) fall through to `_ => false`, and `patterns()` (777-786) both hard-codes four regex sources and silently drops any pattern that fails to compile via `filter_map(...ok())`. The failure mode is therefore a silent reject-all for the affected field rather than a generation error. The current graph is complete (only int/min/max/finite/multipleOf/regex/uuid/email/url/datetime kinds and exactly four regex sources are present, all handled), so there is no present defect; the gap is that the project's own standard for the 69 semantic bindings (tools/generate_validation.py pins and verifies every binding) is not applied to schema checks, and a nested, non-root node introducing a fifth pattern could escape the oracle corpus.
findings.required_fix: Add an inventory assertion in tools/generate_models.py (or generate_validation.py --check) that the set of `checks[].kind` values and `$regexp` sources present in the compacted graph is exactly the set implemented by validation.rs, failing generation on any addition, mirroring the existing semantic-binding verification.

findings.description: Public union models use positional variant names (`Variant1`..`Variant32`, plus `Unknown`), for example `GatewayInferenceResponseStreamEvent::Variant10(GatewayInferenceResponseCompletedEvent)`. Callers must pattern-match opaque ordinals (tests/models/tests.rs:185-192 does exactly this), and because the names encode source order rather than meaning, any upstream reordering renumbers variants so the same name silently denotes a different contract across a regeneration. docs/MODELS.md does not record this naming rule or its stability implications, and nothing in the gate pins variant index to schema identity.
findings.required_fix: Derive variant names from the inner type or discriminator literal (for example `Completed(GatewayInferenceResponseCompletedEvent)`); if positional names are retained, document the rule in docs/MODELS.md and add a generator check that each union's variant index-to-schema mapping is stable against the committed ledger.

findings.description: In the `ZodRecord` arm the normalized key returned by `self.walk(child(node, "key")?, Some(&key_value), depth + 1)?` is discarded, and the original raw key is re-copied into the output at line 437. If a record key schema ever carries a transform or default, the native output would diverge from Zod while still reporting success. No current schema does this, so the oracle corpus cannot detect the divergence.
findings.required_fix: Use the normalized key value when inserting into the result map (falling back to the raw key only when the key schema is an unconstrained string), or assert in the generator that no ZodRecord key schema carries an effect/default.

findings.description: `BinaryFile::new` accepts arbitrarily large `Bytes` with no bound; the size check lives only in `validate(max_bytes)` (line 337), which no currently implemented operation calls because multipart encoders belong to a later phase. docs/MODELS.md:56 states "`BinaryFile` owns bounded bytes", which overstates the constructor's guarantee.
findings.required_fix: Either apply an explicit default ceiling in `new` (callers can raise it via an explicit constructor) or reword docs/MODELS.md:56 to say that byte bounds are applied by `validate(max_bytes)` at the owning operation rather than at construction.

findings.description: An event named `error` is turned into a Protocol failure before the terminal policy is consulted, so a frame carrying `event: error` together with `data: [DONE]` fails in Rust while the frozen parser treats `[DONE]` as a clean terminator first (.local/typescript/src/http/event-stream.ts:137-150) and only raises on a named error event with a non-empty, non-sentinel payload. The ordering difference is safe-by-default but is not listed among the recorded Rust adaptations in docs/STREAMING.md:37-41.
findings.required_fix: Either evaluate the terminal policy before the error-name check to match the baseline ordering, or record the inverted precedence in docs/STREAMING.md as a deliberate difference.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-03.json:3-6 records source_sha256 18bcfea7ac50002482005b7cd811c0fa25111ea38c129d058b05a63efcf5176d (matching the reviewed source SHA supplied for this review), source_unchanged true, passed true; its 26 command entries correspond one-for-one to tools/check_phase.py:47-71 (7 phase-1 commands + generate_validation --check, generate_models --check, native_operations --check, test_native_operations, schema-oracle --check, tsc, 6 toolchain/feature matrices, json-unification, scan/management/gateway/models single-feature builds, generate_models --verify-fixtures, check-package), every one exit_code 0.

Real cargo output, not claims: docs/checks/phase-03-rust-1.99.0-all.json:84 shows `test result: ok. 111 passed` (unit), 15 (representative_clients), 7 (scan_contracts), 5 (schema_contracts), 1 doctest, with fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/doc all exit 0 on x86_64-unknown-linux-musl; the per-feature reports show the expected gating (scan build: 7 scan_contracts, 0 representative_clients; minimal: 5 schema_contracts only; gateway: 11 representative_clients).

Independent oracle comparison is executed, not asserted: crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:74-128 parses every root's jsonCases through validation::parse in both Mode::Request and Mode::Response, compares success *and* normalized output against the fixture's `zod`/`response` expectations, and asserts the checked count equals counts.jsonCases; tools/schema-oracle.mts --check recorded jsonCases 60271, acceptedJsonCases 12956, rejectedJsonCases 47315, unresolvedValidSpecimens [], rootsWithoutJsonRejection []. schema_contracts.rs:19-72 additionally asserts 1086 unique public schema names, 1125 module declarations, 69 manual semantic nodes each with frozen expression evidence, and 10 native boundary bindings.

Scan wire contracts are checked against the frozen fixture, independently of the implementation: tests/scan_contracts.rs:29-42 pins contracts/fixtures/typescript/test/openapi/fixtures/scan.json by sha256 and asserts 4 cases; assert_wire (104-176) compares method, path, host, the full ordered query pair list against `queryWire` (which contains the comma-joined duplicate IDs at fixture lines 351-353 and 559-561), the *exact sorted set* of header names for body and bodyless requests, single-valued headers, service-name: api, the PAN-AIRS/<version>-rust-sdk User-Agent, is_sensitive on every value, the exact request body against the frozen `body`, and x-payload-hash against an HMAC-SHA256 recomputed in the test over the transmitted bytes with the API key.

Phase-3 security behaviours are covered by named, executed tests: invalid_scan_inputs_are_rejected_without_dispatch (scan_contracts.rs:283-350) asserts zero transport calls for every invalid profile/content/batch/ID case; sync_and_async_ambiguous_failures_remain_unknown_and_are_never_replayed (382-438) proves a retry override of 5 still produces exactly one dispatch per paid POST with RemoteOutcome::Unknown and no credential in diagnostics; malformed_known_response_fields_are_rejected_safely (352-363) proves Decode without echoing the rejected value; invalid_pagination_is_rejected_before_token_or_network_work (representative_clients.rs:271-292) asserts provider.calls == 0.

Every attempt-01 blocking/medium finding is fixed in the reviewed source: service-name and User-Agent are now SDK-owned defaults on every assembled request (engine.rs:22-32) and are unoverridable (forbidden_header, engine.rs:118-137); exact header-name sets are asserted in both test suites (scan_contracts.rs:126-140, representative_clients.rs:143-157); ContractStream now skips empty-data keepalives with a dedicated test (streaming.rs:47-76, typed_stream_skips_interleaved_empty_data_keepalives_and_reaches_terminal); Intersection now merges recursively under explicit depth/node/byte bounds with conflict tests (models/support.rs:125-221, models/tests.rs:353-396); the unreachable finite_json arms and unbounded safe_json are gone from validation::apply (669-775); single-product feature builds were added to the gate (check_phase.py:66-68).

Baseline parity spot-checks against the frozen reference: scan paths and region endpoints match constants.ts:8-16,72-75; MAX_CONTENT_* 2 MiB/2 MiB/100 MiB and the 5/5/20 caps match constants.ts:24-42; ScanRequestSchema's tr_id/session_id max(100) is enforced through request-mode validation rather than duplicated locally (scan-request.ts:23-31); /v1/mgmt/profiles with offset/limit/optional latest matches profiles.ts:43-58; /chat/completions and /files/{id}/content match inference-client.ts:423 and runtime-resources-client.ts:445; the HMAC header set matches http/auth/api-key.ts:33-45.

Reproducibility and honesty of bookkeeping: tools/generate_models.py:842-852 compares every generated output byte-for-byte under --check (schema_graph.json, 14 Rust outputs, native-models.json) using pinned rustfmt +1.99.0; contracts/native-operations.json summary records implemented 7 / pending 441 / liveVerified 0 with per-row owningPhase, and docs/phase-status.json keeps phase 3 `in_progress` with live_acceptance `pending_phase_8`; README.md:11-14 makes no release or parity claim.
limitations: Read-only review with no execution: I could not recompute the source-tree SHA-256 or hash docs/checks/phase-03.json, so I cannot independently confirm the supplied 18bcfea7… source digest or the bb99f9… check-file digest. I verified that the check report's own recorded source_sha256 equals the supplied value and that its command list matches tools/check_phase.py exactly.

Recorded check reports are treated as faithful transcripts. Their stdout is detailed and internally consistent with the source I read (test names, counts, feature gating), but as docs/PHASES.md itself notes, these hashes detect staleness rather than authenticate the process.

I did not read all of crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs (over 109,000 lines, 3,261 public types). I inspected representative generated structs and unions and relied on the byte-exact generator --check plus the 27,216-case typed consumer oracle for the remainder.

The response-mode half of contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json comes from a documented widening policy layered over real Zod execution; a systematic error in that policy would be invisible to the Rust comparison. The request-mode half is unmodified frozen Zod output.

All recorded Rust execution is x86_64-unknown-linux-musl only. Other declared target triples, remote CI, and dependency-advisory scanning remain recorded as deferred limitations due in phase 8 and were not assessed here.

No live service acceptance exists or was attempted; every artifact is offline and credential-free. Live scan/management/gateway qualification is explicitly deferred to phase 8 and I treated it as out of scope, as directed.
I inspected no credential or tenant-registration files and nothing outside this repository; .local/typescript was read only as the permitted frozen nonsecret baseline reference.

Performance characteristics were not measured. The response path decodes bytes to serde_json::Value, validates into a second Value, then deserializes into the typed model, and each Optional/Nullable/Patch field buffers through Value; this is a deliberate safety-first design but no benchmark evidence exists for large (multi-MiB) payloads.
